name: Self-Adaptive In-Context Learning: An Information Compression Perspective for In-Context Example Selection and Ordering
venue: ACL 2023 (Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the ACL, Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 1423-1436). First posted to arXiv Dec 2022 (arXiv:2212.10375).
authors_affiliation: Zhiyong Wu (Shanghai AI Lab), Yaoxiang Wang (Xiamen University), Jiacheng Ye (The University of Hong Kong), Lingpeng Kong (The University of Hong Kong). Equal contribution among Wu/Wang/Ye; Wu led the project.
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper repo, last pushed 2023-05-05, ~45 stars, not a maintained leaderboard/paper list)
task_domain: QA / NLP classification and reasoning: in-context-learning (ICL) demonstration selection and ordering for text classification (sentiment, topic), natural language inference, and multi-choice commonsense QA.
problem_setting: Offline, single-model, single-turn ICL with a frozen causal PLM (no parameter updates). The goal is per-test-instance ('self-adaptive') selection AND ordering of k in-context examples, framed as an NP-hard combinatorial optimization / search problem. A key assumption is that NO labeled validation set is required at test time (validation-free); only an unlabeled annotated retrieval pool of candidate examples is available. Supervision: none for the selection/ranking algorithm itself (the retrieval pool provides labeled exemplars but the ranker is unsupervised). Contrasted explicitly with corpus-level methods that pick one universal prompt for all test samples.
what_is_retrieved: In-context demonstrations (labeled input-output examples) from an annotated candidate/training pool, then organized (selected and permuted) per test sample.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed annotated pool of labeled training examples. No growing/episodic memory is written; the pool is frozen.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed-size selection (top-k / fixed candidate-set then fixed-size organization, e.g. 8 examples per prompt). Not a completeness or precision-driven variable-size objective; the contribution is ranking/ordering of fixed-k organizations rather than recovering a minimal complete set.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration (a labeled input-output example); the operative unit for ranking is an 'organization' = an ordered set/permutation of k single demos.
index_source: Static corpus (annotated training/retrieval pool); offline-fixed. No online or test-time induction of the store; the pool is built once and frozen. Selection (e.g. TopK candidates) is computed per test sample at inference but the underlying store does not grow.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index over example embeddings (semantic-similarity nearest-neighbor search via a sentence encoder). VoteK adds diversity-aware graph-style penalization and DPP imposes a determinantal-set structure, but the base index is flat dense.
retriever_type: Two-stage: (1) selection module is dense embedding-based nearest-neighbor (TopK), or diversity-aware variants VoteK and DPP; (2) ranking module is LLM-as-scorer (the frozen PLM itself scores candidate organizations via an MDL/codelength criterion). No learned/trained retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The selection retriever uses fixed semantic similarity (and optionally diversity heuristics). The ranking criterion is an unsupervised information-theoretic objective (Minimum Description Length / codelength, instantiated as the entropy of the PLM's predictive distribution over labels) computed from the frozen PLM's own confidence — no contrastive training, no LM-feedback fine-tuning, no RL, no downstream-label supervision.
query_construction: Raw test input x is used directly as the query for nearest-neighbor selection. For ranking, each candidate organization c is concatenated with the test input and scored by the PLM; the 'query' for MDL is the model's predictive distribution p(y_i | c, x) over candidate labels.
query_granularity: Task/instance-level, one-shot at t=0 (a single per-test-sample query for selection and a single per-test-sample ranking pass; no step-wise or trajectory-level retrieval).
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: a single selection + ranking pass per test instance before generating the prediction. No iterative or uncertainty-triggered re-retrieval during decoding.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (always retrieve once per test sample). No dynamic trigger.
reranking: Yes. The core contribution is the ranking (rerank) stage: after the selection module returns a small candidate set, a window of W candidate organizations (default 10 sampled permutations of 8 examples drawn from ~30 retrieved candidates) is reranked by the MDL/codelength criterion; the lowest-codelength (minimum-entropy) organization is chosen. It is an LLM-confidence-based reranker, not a trained cross-encoder.
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank (MDL-based selection of the best organization among sampled permutations). No decomposition, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of the demonstration content itself.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the chosen organization (ordered concatenation of input-output examples wrapped in a template) is prepended to the test input as the ICL context; the frozen PLM then generates/scores the label. No training signal, no skill reuse, no latent injection.
planning_integration: One-shot exemplars at plan/prediction time. No planning, tree search, or interleaving; retrieval+ranking happens once, then a single forward pass produces the answer.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer (one retrieval-and-rank pass per final prediction; no CoT-step or token-level interleaving).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw input-output demonstration pairs wrapped in a task template (verbatim ICL exemplars). No distillation into strategies/guidelines/programs.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw single demonstrations (concrete labeled examples), assembled into a raw ordered exemplar sequence; no abstraction into distilled strategy/workflow/skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Implicit via the MDL/minimum-entropy ranking objective, which selects the organization making the PLM most confident, thereby down-weighting organizations that produce a flat/uncertain (noisy) predictive distribution. Diversity-aware selection (VoteK, DPP) also reduces redundant/biased candidates. No retriever-aware training, self-reflection module, or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: none (static annotated retrieval pool; no episodic/skill/workflow memory).
write_back: false. No new experiences/cases/skills are written back; the candidate pool is fixed.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store does not grow during deployment/test time; it is frozen after the annotated pool is fixed.
failure_experience_usage: Not applicable / none stored. The method does not store failed or negative experiences. (Note: a separate analysis section studies the effect of corrupting demonstration labels on accuracy, but this is diagnostic, not a stored-failure-retrieval mechanism.)
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no memory entries are written or mutated; the pool is append-free and frozen).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Selection is fixed similarity/diversity heuristics (TopK/VoteK/DPP) and ranking is a fixed unsupervised MDL criterion; neither is an RL-/value-learned policy. The paper explicitly leaves learned selection (e.g. Rubin et al. 2022 EPR) as future work to close the gap to finetuning.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-model, single-instance use; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: Eight NLP datasets: SST-2 and SST-5 (sentiment classification); SNLI, MNLI, QNLI (natural language inference); CommonsenseQA / CMS QA (multi-choice commonsense QA); TREC and AgNews (topic classification).
benchmark_family: QA / NLP-classification (sentiment + topic classification, natural language inference, multi-choice commonsense QA). Not an agentic/web/embodied/tool benchmark; these are GLUE-style and SST/TREC/AgNews/CommonsenseQA classification tasks.
baselines: Three groups. Prompting (zero-shot, no in-context examples). Corpus-level: Random, Random&Validation, MI / Mutual Information (Sorensen et al. 2022, validation-free), GlobalE (Lu et al. 2022, needs validation set). Instance-level: Random (8 random examples per test sample), TopK (Liu et al. 2022), Majority vote (over 8 TopK-retrieved examples), TopK+LocalE (Lu et al. 2022). Proposed: TopK+MDL (Ours).
key_metrics: Accuracy (classification accuracy averaged over 3 random seeds). Also reports average MDL/codelength per method (intrinsic ranking-criterion value) and an oracle upper-bound accuracy.
headline_result: TopK+MDL (Ours) achieves an average accuracy of 60.16 over the eight datasets, a 40% relative improvement over the common-practice Random baseline (corpus-level Random AVG 42.78 / instance-level Random AVG 43.06); and ~17% relative improvement over the instance-level TopK+LocalE baseline (AVG 51.36).
ablations: Multiple analyses: (1) Selection-method comparison — TopK vs VoteK vs DPP; TopK best on average for small-label-space classification, but VoteK/DPP outperform TopK on large-label-space CommonsenseQA. (2) Ranking accuracy vs an oracle (if any of the sampled organizations yields the correct answer): large gap between oracle and TopK+MDL, motivating better rankers/supervised retrieval. (3) Window size W (number of permutations ranked per sample) from 2 to 50: accuracy steadily increases with W (even W=2 gives +3.19 acc on SST-2 over TopK), trading efficiency for effectiveness. (4) Number of in-context examples N from 0 to 32: increasing N helps on average; Random plateaus at N=8 while organization matters. (5) Model scale (OPT 350M to 175B): larger is not always better (plateau on simple tasks; 30B beats 175B on SNLI) but the method improves consistently over baselines at all scales. (6) Generality across PLMs and across prompt templates: consistently beats TopK. (7) Average MDL table showing lower codelength correlates with higher accuracy. (8) Label-corruption / bias-rate analysis on the role of labels.
evaluation_decoupling: Partially. The paper reports the intrinsic ranking criterion (average MDL/codelength per method) and an oracle ranking-accuracy upper bound separately from end-to-end task accuracy, but does not report standard Recall@k/nDCG retrieval metrics (the selection retriever is off-the-shelf).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final task accuracy). Process-side signals reported are the average MDL/codelength of organizations and an oracle upper bound on ranking quality, used to argue that the ranker is the bottleneck.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Explicitly discussed as an efficiency-effectiveness trade-off: the ranking window size W equals the number of forward passes over the test set (W=50 means 50x inference forward passes), so larger W boosts accuracy but multiplies inference cost. Default W=10. Selection reduces the combinatorial search space (e.g. 8-of-10 permutations = A(10,8) ~ 1.8M choices) by retrieving ~30 candidates and sampling 10 permutations to rank. No latency-in-seconds or API-dollar numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: default 8 in-context examples per organization; selection retrieves ~30 nearest candidates, then a window of W=10 randomly sampled 8-example permutations is reranked by MDL and the best chosen (reranked-then-selected, fixed-k). N varied 0-32 and W varied 2-50 in ablations. No explicit token-budget cap.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (research method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing public datasets, not a newly constructed benchmark). Dataset splits are documented (e.g. SST-2 6920/872/1821; SNLI 550152/10000/10000; AgNews 120000/0/7600; CMS QA 9471/1221/1140); for datasets with restricted test access (MNLI, QNLI, CMS QA) a 10% held-out training subset is used for corpus-level validation and results are reported on the validation set.
builds_on: TopK semantic-similarity demonstration retrieval (Liu et al. 2022, 'What makes good in-context examples for GPT-3?'); VoteK selective annotation (Su et al. 2022); determinantal point processes / k-DPP (Kulesza & Taskar 2011) for diverse selection; Minimum Description Length principle (Grunwald 2007) and Solomonoff's theory of inductive inference (1964); description-length-of-deep-learning view (Blier & Ollivier 2018); ICL-as-implicit-Bayesian-inference (Xie et al. 2021).
contrasts_with: Corpus-level prompt/order search methods: GlobalE / LocalE (Lu et al. 2022, 'Fantastically ordered prompts'), Mutual Information prompt selection (Sorensen et al. 2022). Contrasted because those operate at corpus level (one universal prompt for all samples), suffer majority bias, and (GlobalE) require a labeled validation set, whereas this work is per-instance and validation-free. Also contrasts with template-search methods (Gao et al. 2021 LM-BFF, AutoPrompt/Shin et al. 2020, RLPrompt/Deng et al. 2022) that search templates rather than example organization. Positioned against learned-retrieval (Rubin et al. 2022 EPR) as a future complement.
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval). An early (2022/2023) instance-level, training-free demonstration selection-AND-ordering method that introduces an information-compression (MDL) criterion; a predecessor in the lineage of per-query demonstration organization that later learned/RL-based demonstration retrievers build upon.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning method). At most realizes a Retrieve phase (no Reuse-as-adaptation, Revise, or Retain).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is grounded in information theory (MDL) and ICL example-selection literature.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools; demonstrations are raw labeled examples wrapped in task templates, not engineered tool descriptions).
index_content_separation: N/A (no lightweight-index-then-content separation; embeddings index the same examples used as content).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or integration protocol).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; retrieved examples are used as verbatim ICL exemplars without revision).
